We propose and evaluate several novel mechanisms to overlap reads with writes in PCM-based main memory.

the proposed techniques can boost the intra-rank level parallelism during writes in PCM-based main memory from an average of 2.5 to 4.5 (out of a max. of 8.5) across a wide spectrum (including both multithreaded and multi-programmed workloads), resulting in an average IPC boost of 15.7% and 16% for the two types of workloads.
In summary, our research is concerned with
making PCM a more practical main memory technology.
boosting the intra-rank access parallelism during a PCM write to improve performance and energy efficiency.
making PCM more competitive with DRAM in the main memory arena.

the performance of PCM-based memory can be substantially improved by allowing concurrent reads and writes to be serviced during the long latency writes.
